image_description: A dorsal view of a chiton (polyplacophore) clinging to a surface. The organism displays an elongated oval shape with eight distinct, overlapping calcareous plates (valves) arranged in a linear series from anterior to posterior. The plates are greyish-green with vertical striations and dark central markings. They are surrounded by a thick, textured, brownish leathery girdle (mantle) that forms the outer border. The image appears to be a scientific illustration or a high-contrast photograph with a white background.

The edges between the individual plates are slightly soft and lack the sharp, hard definition expected of calcareous structures, suggesting slight generative smoothing.
